messages:
hannah-support: hey team, urgent customer escalation — tenant 'acme-ads' seeing consistent 502/504s for hosted inference since 10:12 UTC. multiple requests timing out. customer says initial requests succeed then huge spike in timeouts. correlation id: cid-8a3f. can oncall triage?

eric-oncall: got it. looking at gateway logs now. I see 504s from the tenant's gateway with backend 'hosted-inference-prod' returning 504 due to upstream timeout at 10:12:30 -> 10:14:00.

eric-oncall: quick grep in router: `grep cid-8a3f /var/log/gateway/* | head` shows repeated `upstream deadline exceeded` and `no healthy upstream` for that tenant.

maya-ml: tagging in — could be scale-up lag. I pulled the model-init logs for that tenant pool and see multiple `model init started` followed by long `loading weights` times (~35s). Our readiness probe timeout is 20s so pods fail readiness until backend is fully warmed.

noah-infra: checking autoscaler metrics. KEDA ScaledObject for tenant-acme seems to have stopped firing around 10:08. KEDA logs show `auth: token unauthorized` on scaler fetch attempts.

billing: heads up — we rotated the aggregator token at 09:55 as part of scheduled key rotation. I pushed the new token to secret `keda/scaler-token` but I see the scaledobject is still referencing the old secret name `billing/old-scaler-token` in the cluster.

eric-oncall: aha. so KEDA's HTTP scaler requests to billing/metrics endpoint returned 401/403, scaler didn't scale, HPA never saw demand until queue blew up. that matches the customer pattern.

maya-ml: combined with slow model warmup that's a recipe for timeouts. readiness probe fails, KEDA doesn't request new replicas, traffic piles into the few warmed pods and upstream hits deadline.

sre-lead: good catch. immediate mitigation: (1) patch ScaledObject to point to new secret name; (2) temporarily increase Deployment replicas for tenant-acme to 3; (3) raise readiness probe timeout to 60s for this tenant model. I'll run the first two now.

noah-infra: commands I'm running:
```
kubectl patch scaledobject tenant-acme-scaledobject --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/triggers/0/authParams/secretKey","value":"new-scaler-token"}]' -n hosted-tenants
kubectl scale deployment hosted-inference-acme --replicas=3 -n hosted-tenants
```

eric-oncall: deploy-bot shows a quick patch deploy event: deploy-bot: `Applied patch to tenant-acme-scaledobject (rev 2026-03-17T10:20)` :white_check_mark:

billing: confirmed secret `new-scaler-token` exists and has valid creds. KEDA should authenticate now. I'll monitor KEDA logs for successful fetch.

noah-infra: KEDA logs now show `scaler: matched metric, triggering scale` at 10:22:12 and HPA increased desired replicas to 4.

maya-ml: new pods are initializing, but model init is still slow (~30s). readiness probe still failing on previous pods, but recent pods eventually pass. recommending we later revisit model init perf and consider background warmup or prefetching.

hannah-support: updated customer at 10:26 — they report error rate dropping, requests start succeeding again. asked customer for sample request that timed out, saved for repro. they need an RCA and mitigation plan.

sre-lead: short RCA notes for later: root cause chain = scheduled billing token rotation + stale secret reference in ScaledObject -> KEDA authentication failures -> no scaler-driven scale-up during burst -> small warm pool + slow model init -> readiness timeouts -> upstream 5xx/504 at gateway. Contributing config issues: ScaledObject secret name not templated, readiness probe timeout too aggressive for that model, no minReplicas/reserved burst capacity for this tenant.

maya-ml: repro steps I used:
1) set scaledobject auth token to invalid -> `kubectl patch`
2) fire burst load with ab: `ab -n 200 -c 50 https://api.redwood.example/v1/hosted/acme/predict`
3) observe KEDA logs show `auth 401` and no scale events, HPA stays at 1, gateway returns 504s after queue timeout.

noah-infra: follow-up remediation items:
- patch ScaledObject to use Kubernetes secret name from central rotator and add a CI lint to catch stale secret refs
- adjust KEDA polling interval to be more aggressive for high-throughput tenants (e.g. 10s -> 5s) while we evaluate cost impact
- set minReplicas=2 for tenant-acme and other high-SLA tenants
- increase readiness probe timeout for known slow models or implement a prewarm hook that loads weights on pod start asynchronously

billing: I'll add a post-rotation checklist to verify ScaledObject refs and run a quick smoke with KEDA test harness for next rotation.

sre-lead: assigning follow-ups: noah -> secret templating + CI lint; maya -> prewarm design doc + probe tuning; billing -> rotation checklist; eric -> write incident summary and customer-facing RCA. target: ship fixes in next 48h and update customer SLA.

eric-oncall: I'll draft the RCA and ping legal/customer success for the external note. leaving this thread open until RCA posted. :thumbsup:
